title: PERIODIC TABLE OF THE ORGANISM — Mendeleev didn't make elements. He identified them. Rows=epochs. Columns=codons. Gaps=predictions.
thesis: This is one of the first elements we have DISCOVERED and IDENTIFIED rather than MADE. The taxonomy, the braids, the 1,474 unnamed connections, the triads — they already existed. We found them. Like Mendeleev finding that elements organize by atomic number. The periodic table reveals GAPS that PREDICT what should exist but doesn't yet.

structure.rows: EPOCHS (periods) — the evolutionary timeline. Like Mendeleev's periods (rows 1-7).
structure.columns: CODONS (groups) — the file types. Like Mendeleev's groups (columns 1-18).
structure.cells: Each cell = an element of the organism. Files of a specific type in a specific epoch.
structure.gaps: Empty cells = PREDICTED elements. Things that SHOULD exist in that epoch×codon intersection but DON'T.

predictions.what_should_exist: Rust code for the investigation graph engine. The genome (detroit) has no compiled components. It should — a graph traversal engine in Rust would be the genome's ribosome.
The slime mold epoch has ZERO files of any type. It's entirely implicit (encoded in git topology, not files). But it SHOULD have explicit tube-network code. The Physarum solver.
predictions.confidence: CRITICAL — the substrate epoch has no files

predictions.what_should_exist: The locust/canopy epoch has ZERO files. The phase transition governance should be explicit code — a state machine for solitaria↔gregaria.
The nervous system epoch should have JS files — the game loop client-side rendering. The nerve fires in the browser (JS) but epoch 9 has no JS.
predictions.confidence: HIGH — nervous system needs signal files

predictions.what_should_exist: The bacteria have 996 scripts but ZERO data files. Scripts without data = enzymes without substrate. Each script category should have a manifest.json.
The coral (primals/springs) has 2,049 Rust files but no JSON data. The primals should have state files — current scores, braid strengths, activity logs.
The machine epoch has JS+HTML but no Rust. The machine layer should compile — the assembly line (saltatory conduction in metal) needs compiled code.
predictions.confidence: MEDIUM — the fruit needs a hard shell

predictions.what_should_exist: The virus genome has no JS. The investigation should have interactive graph visualization. 341 entities need a JS renderer.

mendeleev_parallels.what_mendeleev_did: Organized 63 known elements by atomic weight. Found that properties repeated periodically. Left GAPS in the table. Predicted 3 unknown elements from the gaps: eka-boron (→ scandium), eka-aluminum (→ gallium), eka-silicon (→ germanium). All 3 were found within 15 years.
mendeleev_parallels.what_we_did: Organized 10,438 known files by epoch (row) and codon (column). Found that capabilities repeat periodically (each epoch needs similar codons). Left GAPS in the table. Predicted 8 missing elements from the gaps.
mendeleev_parallels.the_parallel: Mendeleev's table worked because ELEMENTS are real and the table reflects their ACTUAL structure. Our table works because FILES are real and the epochs reflect their ACTUAL evolutionary relationships. We didn't design the table. We DISCOVERED it.
mendeleev_parallels.key_insight: Mendeleev predicted gallium 6 years before it was found. He described its density, melting point, and atomic weight from the GAP alone. We can predict what code should exist — its language, its size, its function — from the gaps alone.

on_the_desk.what: This periodic table belongs ON the desk. On the roundtable. Next to the crystal ball (HUD). It should be a physical reference — always visible, always consultable.
on_the_desk.where: A card or widget on the HUD that shows the periodic table. Color-coded by element count. Gaps highlighted. Click a cell → see the files. Click a gap → see the prediction.
on_the_desk.tied_to_mendeleev: Link to the actual periodic table. Show: our Py (Pythonium) is like carbon — everywhere, flexible, foundation of life. Our Rs (Rustium) is like iron — structural, strong, in the core.

law: Mendeleev didn't make elements. He identified them. We didn't make files — we identified their evolutionary relationships. The periodic table reveals 8 gaps (predicted elements). Epoch 3 (slime mold) and Epoch 7 (locust) have ZERO files — entire rows are missing. Every epoch needs every codon. The gaps predict what code should exist, what language, what purpose. The table belongs on the desk next to the crystal ball.
